title: Handoff Mechanism
eyebrow: Build plan detail · session handoff, issue #406

short.lead: This page shows how each of the five build steps works, with one diagram per step, in the order they would be built. It adds detail to the build plan page and changes none of its steps. The automatic save reuses the subagent autosave that already exists in scripts/house_rules/delegation.py. The save check adds to the existing end-of-reply hook, and the pickup is a new session-start entry. One finding from reading main: the first October design-loop bug (#409) is already fixed by #403.
short.hint: Tap a step to see its diagram, how it works, and when it counts as done.
items: Step 5: automatic save on every branch

Trigger: the existing after-tool hook entry for Write, Edit, NotebookEdit and Bash. Today it stops unless the branch name starts with worktree-agent-. That test goes, so every branch is saved; a detached HEAD is skipped and said once. To stay cheap, the hook first reads one small timestamp file in the .git folder. If the last save was under 60 seconds ago, it only notes the file name and stops, without starting git. Otherwise it builds the snapshot in a temporary index: a copy of the last commit, plus changes to tracked files, plus new files the agent wrote (the #477 rule, so a stray secrets file is never pushed), plus the facts file. The facts are the branch, the last commit, unpushed commits, uncommitted files, the design-loop stage, the stage file's issues and the time. The snapshot becomes a commit that no branch points at, stored at refs/house-rules/autosave/<branch>, and that one ref is pushed with a 6-second timeout. The end of a turn (Stop) and a turn cut off by an error such as a usage limit (StopFailure) get new entries that save at once, skipping the 60-second wait. Work-in-progress commits stay on subagent branches only.

Done when verify.py finds the snapshot after an edit on an AjsAgent/ branch and after an edit on main, confirms the branch, staging area and folder are unchanged, and a live edit makes the ref appear on GitHub.

items.alt: Flow of the automatic save from an edit to a pushed snapshot
items.caption: The automatic save. Orange is what it never changes.

items: This is a new row in the existing end-of-reply hook (event_handover in scripts/hook.py). It runs only when the turn wrote a file or made a commit, which the hook already works out. It asks five questions. Is every file the turn wrote committed? This is the existing commit check. Is the branch pushed, with an upstream and nothing left to push? On main, the advice is to branch off first. Is the handoff note docs/5-today/handoff-<branch>.md no older than the newest commit? Is the note free of published page links, session links and Claude credit? And did docs/5-today/Today.md change in a turn that changed other files? Any no sends the reply back once with the exact fix, through the existing one-block checkpoint. A git error counts as "could not tell" and is said, never treated as a pass. HOUSE_RULES_HANDOFF=off turns it off.
Done when verify.py replays each case (unpushed branch, stale note, forbidden link, Today.md untouched, nothing changed, fully saved) and gets the expected block or silence.

items.alt: The five end-of-reply checks and their two outcomes
items.caption: The end-of-reply check, kept as a backstop behind the automatic save.

items: This is a new session-start entry of its own, like the existing issue list, because the main rules entry is close to its size limit. In a git repo, it fetches refs/house-rules/autosave/* from GitHub into a separate place (refs/house-rules/remote-autosave/), so nothing local is overwritten, with a 5-second limit. It also fetches the current branch to count how many commits this folder is behind. That is the check that would have caught today's stale folder. It shows three things: the committed handoff note, the facts from the newest snapshot for this branch, and the behind count. Then it compares each file the snapshot changed with the folder. Files that are already the same are skipped. A file only in the snapshot is listed with the restore command (git restore --source=<snapshot> -- <file>), and the agent is told to ask you before running it. A file changed in both places is listed as a conflict and left out of the command. The block is capped in length, and the cut is named. Snapshots of other branches from the last day get one line.

Done when verify.py replays a session start in a fresh clone with a snapshot (the note, the facts and the missing file are shown), one with no snapshot (silent), one with no network (said in one line), and one with an oversized note (cut, and the cut named).

items.alt: Flow of the pickup from session start to the block shown at the top
items.caption: The pickup. Nothing is restored without your yes.

items: Reading main found that bug 1 is already fixed. A feature name now ends at a tag such as </message>, and trailing answer codes are cut (#403, scripts/house_rules/design_loop.py, with a verify.py check). Bug 2 is a quoted message from another thread moving this thread's stage. Main now skips quoted text and helper messages, but no check replays that exact October prompt. So this step adds the replay of both prompts, fixes only what fails, and closes #409 after your QA.
Done when verify.py replays both October prompts: the first saves the name usage limit handoff, and the second moves nothing and says why.

items.alt: Before and after for the two design-loop bugs
items.caption: Bug 1 is fixed on main already; bug 2 gets a replay to confirm.

items: Rules, docs, tests and a real two-account run

The house-rules text gains one line saying work is saved on every edit and picked up at session start. Today.md, ProjectState.md and docs/4-systems/usage-handoff.md are updated, and the plugin version goes up so installs update. verify.py and tools/verify_tools.py are run twice. Then comes the real run. In a session on one Claude account, a file is edited and the session is stopped mid-turn. git ls-remote shows the snapshot on GitHub. A session on a second account opens a fresh clone in a new folder. Its pickup shows the note, the facts and the missing file, and after your yes the file is restored.
Done when that run is recorded with its real output in docs/5-today/Today.md.

items.caption: The real run is the proof; a green test suite alone is not.
